learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the monumental musical treatises that shaped the grammar, rules, and aesthetics of Indian classical music over centuries.

key_vocabulary.definition: An ancient, authoritative text or treatise.
The oldest surviving text on performing arts, authored by Bharat Muni.
A 13th-century comprehensive musical treatise written by Pt. Sarangadeva.
A 17th-century text by Pt. Ahobal that revolutionized the placement of notes on string instruments.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Written between 200 BCE and 200 CE, it is a master manual for theater, dance, and music. It contains 36 chapters, with chapters 28-33 dedicated exclusively to music. It introduced the concept of 'Rasa' (aesthetics/emotion), classified instruments into 4 types (Tat, Sushir, Avanaddha, Ghan), and established the relation between 22 Shrutis (microtones) and 7 Swaras (notes).

Written in the 13th century, it is often called the 'Saptadhyayi' because it has 7 chapters covering Swara, Raga, Prakirnaka (performance), Prabandha (composition), Tala, Vadya (instruments), and Nartana (dance). It bridged the gap between ancient and medieval music, detailing Margi and Desi Sangeet, and documented the 264 Ragas of that time.

Written in 1650 CE, this text is famous for its scientific approach. Ahobal was the first scholar to mathematically establish the placement of the 12 notes (7 pure, 5 modified) on the 36-inch string of the Veena based on string length and tension. He described 122 Ragas and categorized them scientifically.

fun_activity.title: 📏 Ahobal's String Math
fun_activity.instructions: Stretch a rubber band over a hollow box. Pluck it to hear the base note (Sa). Now, press the exact middle of the rubber band and pluck either half. The sound will be exactly one octave higher (Taar Sa)! Pt. Ahobal wrote this mathematical physics rule in the Sangeet Parijat nearly 400 years ago!

exam_tips: 📌 Always associate the author with their text: Bharat Muni $\rightarrow$ Natya Shastra; Sarangadeva $\rightarrow$ Sangeet Ratnakar; Ahobal $\rightarrow$ Sangeet Parijat.
📌 If asked about 'Saptadhyayi', explain that 'Sapta' means 7 and 'Adhyaya' means chapters, referring to the 7 detailed chapters of Sangeet Ratnakar.
📌 Pt. Ahobal's contribution of fixing notes on the Veena string is a guaranteed question for understanding the scientific temper of medieval music.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Natya Shastra is considered the 'Fifth Veda' because of its immense cultural importance.
⭐ Sangeet Ratnakar is the common reference point for both Hindustani and Carnatic music systems before they split.
⭐ Sangeet Parijat was translated into Persian by Deenanath in the 17th century, showing its widespread influence.
